passages.context: Theodorus, Poenitentiale, II, De fornicatione, section 6, printed p. 185 (artifact p. 209). The sentence assigns tariffs and uses mollis inside a sexual classification. It must not be converted into a claim about modern identity categories.
passages.notes: Wasserschleben's adjacent editorial footnote compares the tariff with the adulteress tariff elsewhere; that footnote is not part of the checked passage text.

passages.context: An Anglo-Saxon penitential compilation, canon 60, printed p. 340 (artifact p. 364). Here mollities is paired with infirmity as inability to bear an assigned fast or austerity, and the text permits commutation.
passages.notes: This nonsexual endurance sense is registered specifically to prevent silent harmonization with the sexual-classification uses elsewhere in the same edited collection.

work.description: Wasserschleben's 1851 collection of Latin western penitential texts with a German historical introduction and editorial apparatus. The collection preserves heterogeneous and sometimes composite witnesses; its readings must be attributed to the named penitential and exact locus rather than treated as one universal canonical code.
